name: Energy Capital Partners Management, LP (ECP) — the infrastructure investment platform of Bridgepoint Group plc
headquarters: 40 Beechwood Road, Summit, New Jersey 07901, United States (offices in New York, San Diego and Seoul)
employees: ~95 (57 performing investment advisory functions) per SEC Form ADV, 30 April 2026

ownership.type: subsidiary (Bridgepoint Group plc, LSE: BPT — combination completed 20 August 2024; ECP is Bridgepoint's Infrastructure segment)
ownership.notes: SEC-registered adviser 'ECP' (CRD 155020, SEC file 801-74094). Form ADV Schedule A (30 Apr 2026): owned through Energy Capital Partners Holdings, LP and Holdings II, LP with Bridgepoint Infrastructure GP Limited as general partner; Bridgepoint executives Raoul Hughes and Xavier Robert sit on the board of managers of ECP ControlCo, LLC beside the four ECP partners. Bridgepoint paid GBP 233m cash, 185.0m consideration units and 45.0m earn-out units (vesting to 2029), assuming GBP 179m of ECP debt. Blue Owl Capital held 19.3% of ECP at signing (Public Citizen, 2023), the affiliation that FERC's first order found undisclosed.

summary:
**BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT:** ECP is the corpus's most active seller of power in 2026, not a buyer of equipment. In the eighteen months to October 2026 it sold Calpine to Constellation (closed 7 January 2026; Bridgepoint states USD 33bn of enterprise value at closing, two-thirds paid in Constellation shares), sold Cornerstone's 2.6 GW of PJM gas plants to Talen (closed 15 June 2026 for USD 3,542m, 4.4x its money in under a year) and sold Symmetry to NextEra (9 January 2026, 6.4x), then closed its largest fund, ECP VI, at USD 8.1bn on 6 August 2026 against a USD 5bn target. It is deploying that fund into regulated and contracted assets — Grain LNG (50/50 with Centrica), EnergySolutions (agreed 6 April 2026, pending) and the GBP 5.75bn DCC Energy take-private with KKR (approved by 78.09% of scheme shares on 18 September 2026, completion expected Q1 2027). Its data-centre exposure runs through the USD 50bn partnership with KKR, whose first campus (CyrusOne DFW10, Bosque County, Texas, 190 MW) is due to operate in Q4 2026 beside a Calpine plant that now belongs to Constellation. ECP remains a 4.0% holder of Constellation and a 5.0% holder of Talen, and ProEnergy, its majority-owned turbine platform, is reported to be weighing a USD 40–50bn IPO.

**BACKGROUND.** Founded in 2005 by Doug Kimmelman, ECP has been the Infrastructure segment of Bridgepoint Group plc (LSE: BPT) since the combination completed on 20 August 2024, after FERC declined the first application in March 2024 over an undisclosed Blue Owl affiliation. Per Bridgepoint's filings the segment's AUM was EUR 36.0bn at 31 December 2025 and EUR 27.7bn at 30 June 2026 after the Calpine and Cornerstone exits; ECP's own Form ADV reports regulatory AUM of USD 33.39bn across 64 pooled vehicles. Its flagship funds are ECP III (2014, USD 5.1bn), ECP IV (2018, USD 3.3bn), ECP V (2022, USD 4.4bn; marked at a gross 3.1x) and ECP VI (2026, USD 8.1bn). Bridgepoint recognised carried interest from ECP V for the first time in H1 2026. ECP exited Terra-Gen entirely on 1 October 2024 and held no Sunnova shares before that company's 2025 bankruptcy.
ecosystemRole: We assess ECP as the capital segment's generation-first investor: where its peers reach data centres through landlords, ECP reaches them through power plants and sells the plants into the AI demand wave. The KKR–ECP partnership pairs KKR's data-centre platforms with ECP's generation, and its first campus sits on a Calpine site; the ADQ–ECP partnership (USD 25bn, 25 GW) is built to develop new gas generation for the same load. ECP itself places no equipment orders — the buyers are its platforms (ProEnergy's turbine and bridge-power business, Convergent's storage projects, Atlantica's contracted fleet, the pending EnergySolutions and DCC businesses) and, increasingly, the strategics it sells to (Constellation, Talen, NextEra). A seller meets ECP as a signatory on the capital side of a power deal and as a shareholder of two listed generators it has just created.

productsAndServices.name: ECP flagship infrastructure funds (ECP III–VI)

Bridgepoint's H1 2026 fund table: ECP III (vintage 2014, USD 5.1bn, gross MOIC 2.3x, DPI 1.9x, gross IRR 17.5%); ECP IV (2018, USD 3.3bn plus USD 3.5bn of co-investment, 2.1x, DPI 1.0x, 20.9%); ECP V (2022, USD 4.4bn final close May 2024 plus USD 2.3bn of fee-paying co-investment, 3.1x, DPI 0.6x, 65.4%; 85% deployed). productsAndServices.name: Strategic partnerships — KKR (USD 50bn, data centres and power) and ADQ (USD 25bn, US generation)
productsAndServices.description: Two programme-level partnerships announced in the eighteen months after the Bridgepoint combination. The KKR–ECP strategic partnership (30 October 2024) commits to invest USD 50bn in data centres together with power generation and transmission; KKR funds it from infrastructure, real estate and insurance accounts, ECP 'from existing and future infrastructure capital pools', and the parties cite more than 8 GW of existing data-centre pipeline and 100 GW of operating and development-ready generation. Its first investment, announced 30 July 2025, is a 190 MW hyperscale campus in Bosque County, Texas (CyrusOne's DFW10), built with CyrusOne beside Calpine's Thad Hill Energy Center under a long-term dedicated power contract, with initial IT capacity of 144 MW, a USD 1.2bn first phase and 'total investment approaching $4 billion' at full build-out; operations are expected in Q4 2026. The ADQ–ECP partnership (19 March 2025) is a 50:50 vehicle targeting more than USD 25bn of investment across 25 GW of primarily new-build US gas generation, with an initial USD 5bn contribution; no first investment had been announced by October 2026.
highlights: Bosque County stake splits are not disclosed by any party; CyrusOne states a '190 MW agreement' with Calpine and says the Calpine fleet can deliver 'up to 400 MW to data centers in Bosque'; a project tracker records the first building topped out in March 2026
The campus's power counterparty, Calpine, has been owned by Constellation since 7 January 2026 — ECP now sits on the capital side only
ECP and KKR extended the relationship beyond data centres with the joint GBP 5.75bn offer for DCC Energy plc (July 2026)
productsAndServices.positioning: The partnership is the mirror image of KKR's Helix vehicle: KKR brings landlords (CyrusOne, STTGDC), ECP brings generation. Among the corpus's investors only ECP pairs with a sovereign (ADQ) explicitly to build gas plants for AI load.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Programme agreements funded from the partners' existing funds and separate accounts; not a fund offered to third-party LPs.
productsAndServices.roadmap: Bosque County operations expected Q4 2026 (first-party, July 2025; no later first-party update). ADQ partnership's first project undisclosed.

productsAndServices.name: Power generation platforms — the realised set (Calpine, Cornerstone, Symmetry, Terra-Gen) and the listed stakes they left
productsAndServices.category: Portfolio — power generation and gas supply
productsAndServices.description: ECP's generation franchise has been converted into cash and listed stock since 2024. Calpine (about 23 GW of gas, geothermal, storage and solar, held through ECP III/IV vehicles, the 2022 Calpine Continuation and Rollover Funds and co-investors including CPP Investments and Access Industries) was sold to Constellation: agreed 10 January 2025 for 50 million Constellation shares, about USD 4.5bn of cash and about USD 12.7bn of assumed net debt (an equity purchase price of about USD 16.4bn per Constellation), completed 7 January 2026; Bridgepoint states USD 33bn of enterprise value at closing and that two-thirds of proceeds came as Constellation shares under lock-ups expiring 30 June 2026 (50%) and 30 June 2027 (50%). Cornerstone Generation — Waterford (869 MW) and Darby (480 MW) in Ohio and Lawrenceburg (1,218 MW) in Indiana, the gas plants ECP acquired with the Lightstone portfolio in August 2025 — was sold to Talen: signed 15 January 2026 at USD 3.45bn (about 6.6x 2027E adjusted EBITDA), closed 15 June 2026 at USD 3,542m (USD 2,615m cash plus 2,399,998 Talen shares valued at USD 927m). Symmetry Energy Solutions, a gas supply and logistics platform, was sold to NextEra Energy Resources on 9 January 2026. Terra-Gen was exited entirely when Masdar bought ECP's remaining 50% on 1 October 2024.
highlights: Constellation stake: ECP vehicles held 22,043,724 shares (6.1%) at the 7 January 2026 close; in the 2 June 2026 underwritten offering the Calpine holders sold 11,000,000 shares at USD 281 (USD 279 to the underwriters), Constellation repurchased 2,000,000 of them for about USD 558m, and ECP's holding fell to 14,443,227 shares (4.0%) — 35% of its 2026 tranche sold, the 2027 tranche still locked (Schedule 13G/A, 7 August 2026; Bridgepoint H1 2026)

Talen stake: 2,399,998 shares (5.01% of 47,894,656 outstanding) held through ECP V Cornerstone vehicles under 90- and 180-day lock-ups (Schedule 13G, 23 June 2026); still held at 30 June 2026 and no resale filed through 3 October 2026

What ECP kept from Lightstone: the 2,709 MW General James M. Gavin coal plant in Ohio, which ECP told FERC it would run 'for so long as [it is] legally able to do so on an economic basis'; FERC approved the Lightstone purchase from Blackstone and ArcLight on 23 July 2025 (docket EC24-125)

Returns stated by Bridgepoint: Cornerstone 4.4x after less than a year; Symmetry 6.4x; ECP V marked above 3x; EUR 11bn of the record EUR 16.6bn Bridgepoint returned to fund investors in H1 2026 came from Calpine. Bloomberg's '>USD 5.5bn returned in 2025' is a press figure, not a filing
productsAndServices.positioning: The seller side of the corpus's two largest 2026 generation deals; Talen's Cornerstone purchase and Constellation's Calpine purchase both carry ECP's price.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Sales to listed strategics for cash plus stock, with registration-rights agreements and staged lock-ups; underwritten secondary offerings to monetise.
productsAndServices.roadmap: Remaining Constellation shares unlock 30 June 2027; Talen lock-ups lapsed September and December 2026 — no resale registered as of 3 October 2026.

productsAndServices.name: ProEnergy — majority-owned aeroderivative turbine and bridge-power platform
productsAndServices.description: ECP acquired a majority interest in ProEnergy (Sedalia, Missouri) from affiliates of Eos Partners and ACON Investments on 5 September 2024; terms were undisclosed, and Bloomberg reported in September 2026 that ECP paid about USD 275m for roughly 60%. ProEnergy's PE6000 is a 50 MW aeroderivative unit it describes as interchangeable with the LM6000PC; in April 2026 it announced a 650 MW, thirteen-unit power solution for Crusoe and the divestiture of its Braes Bayou and Brotman generating stations to STEC. Bridgepoint records a 2025 'partial exit from ProEnergy, the first exit from the 2022 vintage ECP V' — the WattBridge peaker fleet — and attributes part of ECP V's carry to 'very strong growth in the order book for the retained gas turbine business'. On 21 September 2026 Bloomberg reported ProEnergy was weighing a US IPO at a USD 40–50bn valuation with Morgan Stanley and JPMorgan, or an outright sale.
highlights: ProEnergy is the one ECP platform in this corpus that both sells equipment (turbines, EPC) and owns bridge-power assets for data centres — the dossier `proenergy` carries the product detail
The reported USD 275m-for-60% entry against a reported USD 40–50bn IPO mark would be the largest mark-up in ECP's history; both figures are Bloomberg's, confirmed by neither ECP nor ProEnergy
productsAndServices.positioning: ECP's route from capital to equipment: its only portfolio company that manufactures and services turbines for AI load.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Majority equity stake held by ECP V vehicles.

productsAndServices.name: Regulated and contracted platforms — Atlantica, Grain LNG, Convergent, and the pending EnergySolutions and DCC Energy acquisitions

strategyRead: **(High confidence)** We assess that **ECP is a seller of power into the AI demand wave, not a builder of data centres**. Basis: in nine months it converted Calpine (USD 33bn EV at close per Bridgepoint), Cornerstone (USD 3,542m) and Symmetry into cash and listed stock, while its only data-centre position is a programme stake in one CyrusOne campus whose power counterparty it no longer owns. The purchase orders a vendor wants are at the buyers of ECP's plants — Constellation and Talen — and at ProEnergy.

**(High confidence)** We assess that **the Lightstone-to-Cornerstone loop is ECP's model in miniature**: buy a portfolio with a coal plant nobody else wants (Gavin), sell the gas plants to a listed IPP at a data-centre premium within a year (4.4x), keep the coal plant and the Talen shares. Basis: FERC's July 2025 approval of the Lightstone purchase and Talen's June 2026 closing documents; Bridgepoint's own money-multiple statement.

**(Moderate confidence)** We assess that **ECP VI's deployment will look less like Calpine and more like Grain LNG and DCC — contracted, regulated, European and co-owned** — because the parent is a London-listed manager whose fee income now depends on fund size and whose network sourced both deals. Basis: the three named Fund VI deployments; Bridgepoint's statement that ECP VII is deferred to 2029 'to allow for deployment of a larger ECP VI'. Cuts against this: the ADQ partnership exists to build new US gas plants, and no first project has been announced after eighteen months.

**(Moderate confidence)** We assess that **ECP retains listed stakes in its buyers by design rather than by lock-up alone**. Basis: it sold only 35% of the Constellation tranche that unlocked in June 2026, kept the entire Talen position past the first lock-up lapse, and Andrew Gilbert described ECP as 'a significant shareholder' of Talen 'excited to enhance our exposure to Ohio's growth'. For a seller, that makes ECP a continuing voice at two strategics it no longer controls. Collection gap: ECP has not stated a holding policy for either stake.

**(Moderate confidence)** We assess that **ProEnergy is the route by which ECP's capital most directly reaches equipment**, and that the reported IPO would list the corpus's turbine-and-bridge-power supplier under ECP's continuing control. Basis: Bridgepoint's attribution of ECP V carry to ProEnergy's turbine order book; the Crusoe 650 MW order; Bloomberg's September 2026 report. The USD 40–50bn valuation and the USD 275m entry price are press figures confirmed by neither party.

**(Low confidence)** We assess that **FERC and congressional scrutiny of private-equity generation ownership is a rising cost for ECP's next US deal**. Basis: FERC's March 2024 refusal of the Bridgepoint combination over the Blue Owl affiliation, the protests against Calpine and Gavin, and the September 2026 bipartisan letter against GIP/AES — none of which has yet named ECP. Treat as a tripwire, not a finding.

**INDICATORS TO WATCH** — *Q4 2026, CyrusOne DFW10 operations in Bosque County:* a first-party operational release would confirm the KKR–ECP thesis; a slip would indicate the partnership's first campus is behind. *2026, EnergySolutions closing:* confirms ECP VI's second deployment. *Q1 2027, DCC Energy scheme effective:* the EC merger and foreign-subsidies clearances are the gates. *Any Talen resale prospectus supplement or Constellation 13G/A:* would show ECP monetising rather than holding. *An S-1 or confidential filing by ProEnergy:* would convert a press report into a listing. *11 March 2027, Bridgepoint FY2026 results:* the next first-party AUM, deployment and carry figures — Bridgepoint publishes no Q3 trading update.

relationships.note: KKR and ECP announced a USD 50bn partnership for data centres with power generation on 30 October 2024; its first campus is CyrusOne's DFW10 in Bosque County; the two also bid jointly for DCC Energy plc in July 2026.
relationships.context:
KKR's 30 October 2024 release states that KKR funds the partnership from its infrastructure, real estate and insurance strategies and ECP 'from existing and future infrastructure capital pools'. The first investment, announced 30 July 2025, is a 190 MW hyperscale campus in Bosque County, Texas, built with CyrusOne beside Calpine's Thad Hill plant, with operations expected in Q4 2026.

On 27 July 2026 Dragon Bidco, indirectly wholly owned by ECP and KKR funds, announced a recommended cash offer for DCC Energy plc of up to 6,797.22p per share, about GBP 5.75bn of equity; 78.09% of scheme shares approved it on 18 September 2026. The ECP/KKR split of the equity is not disclosed in the Rule 2.7 announcement.

relationships.scale: 190 MW campus; 144 MW initial IT; USD 1.2bn first phase
relationships.note: CyrusOne is the developer of DFW10, the first campus of the KKR–ECP partnership, under a 190 MW agreement with Calpine.
relationships.context: CyrusOne's 30 July 2025 release describes a 190 MW agreement with Calpine for a hyperscale campus adjacent to the Thad Hill Energy Center, a USD 1.2bn first phase and operations in Q4 2026; the ECP–KKR release the same day states initial IT capacity of 144 MW and 'total investment approaching $4 billion'. Neither release gives stake percentages. A project tracker records the first building topping out in March 2026; no first-party status update has followed, and Calpine passed to Constellation on 7 January 2026.

relationships.scale: 2,399,998 shares (5.01%) after the USD 3,542m Cornerstone sale
relationships.note: Talen bought Cornerstone Generation (about 2.6 GW of PJM gas) from ECP on 15 June 2026 for USD 2,615m cash plus 2,399,998 shares; ECP V vehicles hold those shares.
relationships.context: Talen's 8-K of 15 June 2026 and its Q2 2026 10-Q record the purchase price of USD 3,542m — cash of USD 2,615m and 2,399,998 shares valued at USD 927m (USD 386.21 at close) — for Waterford, Darby and Lawrenceburg, with a registration rights agreement and 90- and 180-day lock-ups on the stock. ECP ControlCo's Schedule 13G of 23 June 2026 reports 2,399,998 shares, 5.01% of 47,894,656 outstanding, held through ECP V Cornerstone vehicles; no resale filing had appeared by 3 October 2026. Bridgepoint states a 4.4x money multiple after less than a year of ownership.

relationships.scale: 14,443,227 shares (4.0%) after selling about 7.6m in June 2026
relationships.note: ECP sold Calpine to Constellation (closed 7 January 2026) and received Constellation shares as two-thirds of its proceeds; it remains a 4.0% holder under a 2027 lock-up.
relationships.context: Constellation's completion release of 7 January 2026 and the registration rights agreement filed the same day name ECP, CPP Investments and Access Industries as the Calpine holders. ECP ControlCo's Schedule 13G reported 22,043,724 shares (6.1%) at the close. In the underwritten offering of 2 June 2026 the Calpine holders sold 11,000,000 shares at USD 281 (USD 279 to the underwriters) and Constellation repurchased 2,000,000 for about USD 558m; ECP's 13G/A of 7 August 2026 shows 14,443,227 shares (4.0%). Bridgepoint states that 35% of the tranche released in 2026 was sold and the 2027 tranche is held. Bridgepoint states USD 33bn of enterprise value at closing; Constellation's 2025 announcement stated 50 million shares, about USD 4.5bn of cash and about USD 12.7bn of assumed net debt.

relationships.scale: co-owners of Calpine until 7 January 2026; co-sellers of Constellation shares on 2 June 2026
relationships.note: CPP Investments was a Calpine co-owner in the ECP-led consortium and received Constellation shares beside ECP at the January 2026 close.
relationships.context: Constellation's 10 January 2025 announcement names 'Calpine's significant shareholders, including ECP, Canada Pension Plan Investments (CPP Investments) and Access Industries'; the registration rights agreement of 7 January 2026 names Canada Pension Plan Investment Board as a party. In the 2 June 2026 offering CPP Investments sold 2,660,479 shares (plus up to 326,516 option shares) beside ECP's roughly 7.6m. The two also sit on opposite sides of nothing else in this corpus.

relationships.note: Vistra's chairman Scott B. Helm is a former founding partner of ECP, per Vistra's 2026 proxy; he has been a private investor for more than a decade.
relationships.context: Vistra's definitive proxy of 18 March 2026 describes Mr Helm as having 'previously' been 'a founding partner of Energy Capital Partners' and, for over a decade, 'a private investor based out of Baltimore'. He does not appear on ECP's Form ADV Schedule A. The corpus had described him as a current ECP founding partner; the tense is corrected here and in the Vistra dossier.

relationships.note: ECP owned Terra-Gen from 2015 and sold its remaining 50% to Masdar, closing 1 October 2024 — 'ECP has fully exited its position in Terra-Gen'.
relationships.context: The Masdar closing announcement hosted by Terra-Gen states that Masdar completed the acquisition of ECP's 50% interest in Terra-Gen Power Holdings II, LLC on 1 October 2024, that Igneo Infrastructure Partners retains the other 50%, and that ECP has fully exited. The portfolio at the time was 3.8 GW of operating generation including 5.1 GWh of storage across 30 sites.

relationships.scale: Lightstone Generation (Gavin and three Midwest plants), FERC-approved 23 July 2025
relationships.note: ECP bought Lightstone Generation — the Gavin coal plant and the gas plants later sold to Talen as Cornerstone — from Blackstone and ArcLight.
relationships.context: Private Equity Stakeholder Project and the FERC record (docket EC24-125) show ECP acquiring Lightstone Generation from Blackstone and ArcLight, with FERC approval on 23 July 2025; ECP told FERC it would be the only holder of 10% or more of the voting equity. The price was not disclosed. The gas plants in that portfolio (Waterford, Darby, Lawrenceburg) became Cornerstone Generation and were sold to Talen in June 2026; ECP kept Gavin.

relationships.scale: Symmetry Energy Solutions sale, closed 9 January 2026 (6.4x per Bridgepoint)
relationships.note: NextEra Energy Resources bought Symmetry Energy Solutions, ECP's gas supply and logistics platform, in a sale that closed on 9 January 2026.
relationships.context: ECP's release of 9 January 2026 (Business Wire, read via a mirror) records the closing of the sale of Symmetry Energy Solutions — about 5,500 large commercial and industrial customers and more than 80,000 residential and small-business customers across 34 states — to NextEra Energy Resources; terms were undisclosed. Bridgepoint's H1 2026 report states a 6.4x money multiple.

policyExposure.regime: FERC Federal Power Act §203 — change of control over public utilities
policyExposure.exposure: FERC declined ECP's and Bridgepoint's first application (docket EC24-2) on 1 March 2024 for 'insufficient information' on voting restrictions over a minority holder — Blue Owl Capital, which Public Citizen said owned 19.3% of ECP and 15.5% of Bridgepoint; the refiled application (EC24-69, 11 April 2024) was approved and the combination closed on 20 August 2024. Every later ECP transaction has run the same gate: Lightstone/Gavin (EC24-125, approved 23 July 2025), Calpine/Constellation (EC25-43, conditional approval 23 July 2025 with 3,546 MW of PJM divestitures, after Earthjustice and Public Citizen asked FERC to force ECP to divest its Constellation shares) and Cornerstone/Talen (EC26-59, closed 15 June 2026).
policyExposure.mitigation: ECP's filings state its ownership structure in full; the Lightstone application stated ECP would be the only 10%-plus voting holder with exclusive board rights.

policyExposure.regime: US Senate Banking Committee oversight — private-equity ownership of utilities and data centres
policyExposure.exposure: Senator Warren's 10 June 2026 letters to KKR, BlackRock, Brookfield and Blackstone on data-centre ownership cite KKR and GIP's CyrusOne but do not name ECP or the KKR–ECP partnership; the 29 September 2026 bipartisan letter urging FERC to reject the GIP/AES takeover does not name ECP either. ECP is adjacent to both — it funds the campus CyrusOne is building and is itself a private-equity owner of generation.

policyExposure.regime: EU Merger Regulation 139/2004 and Foreign Subsidies Regulation 2022/2560 — DCC Energy
policyExposure.exposure: The DCC Energy scheme is conditional on a European Commission decision under the Merger Regulation, Foreign Subsidies Regulation notifications by both ECP and KKR, Canadian and Turkish competition clearances, a UK CMA briefing paper and Irish High Court sanction; no EC case number had been published by 3 October 2026. The long-stop date is 31 July 2027.

ECP's retained 2,709 MW Gavin coal plant is the target of a Private Equity Stakeholder Project and Sierra Club campaign against Bridgepoint's energy-transition positioning; ECP's December 2024 FERC filing pledged to keep Gavin operating 'for so long as [it is] legally able to do so on an economic basis'.

policyExposure.regime: CFIUS and UK NSI Act — foreign-controlled acquisitions of infrastructure
policyExposure.exposure: Atlantica's take-private by ECP funds and co-investors cleared CFIUS and FERC by 25 October 2024; since 20 August 2024 ECP's ultimate parent is a UK-listed company, so its US acquisitions carry a foreign-parent dimension. Grain LNG's NSI Act treatment is not stated in the sources read.
